mcqs.question: Which of the following pairs of nuclides are isobars?
mcqs.explanation: Isobars are nuclides of different elements that have the same mass number. Carbon-14 and Nitrogen-14 both have a mass number of 14, making them isobars. The other pairs have different mass numbers or are the same element, so they are not isobars.

mcqs.question: Two atoms of an element have 6 protons each. One atom has 6 neutrons, the other has 7 neutrons. Which statement correctly distinguishes isotopes from isobars?

options.A: The two atoms are isotopes because they have the same number of protons but different neutrons.
options.B: The two atoms are isobars because they have the same mass number.
options.C: Isotopes have the same mass number, while isobars have the same atomic number.
options.D: Both terms refer to atoms with the same number of electrons.

mcqs.answer: The two atoms are isotopes because they have the same number of protons but different neutrons.
mcqs.explanation: Isotopes are atoms of the same element (same atomic number) that differ in neutron number, giving different mass numbers. Isobars are atoms of different elements with the same mass number. Here the atoms share the same atomic number (6) and differ in neutrons, so they are isotopes, not isobars.

mcqs.question: The atomic number of an element is defined as:

options.A: Number of protons in the nucleus
options.B: Number of neutrons in the nucleus
options.D: Number of electrons in a neutral atom

mcqs.answer: Number of protons in the nucleus
mcqs.explanation: Atomic number (Z) equals the number of protons in the nucleus and uniquely identifies an element. It also equals the number of electrons in a neutral atom, but the definition is based on protons. Options B, C, and D describe other quantities.

mcqs.question: An atom has 15 protons and 16 neutrons. What is its mass number?
mcqs.explanation: Mass number (A) is the total number of protons and neutrons: A = 15 + 16 = 31. Option A adds incorrectly, while C and D give only one of the components.

mcqs.learning_point: Calculate numbers of protons, electrons and neutrons
mcqs.question: Atom X has 19 protons and a mass number of 39. Atom Y has 19 protons and a mass number of 40. Which statement correctly compares their neutron numbers?

options.A: Both atoms have the same number of neutrons
options.B: Atom X has one more neutron than Atom Y
options.C: Atom Y has one more neutron than Atom X
options.D: Neutron numbers cannot be determined from the given data

mcqs.answer: Atom Y has one more neutron than Atom X
mcqs.explanation: Neutrons = mass number – atomic number. For X: 39‑19 = 20 neutrons. For Y: 40‑19 = 21 neutrons. Therefore Y has one more neutron than X. Options A and B are incorrect, and D is false because the data is sufficient.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about the isotopes of chlorine is correct?

options.A: All isotopes of chlorine have the same number of neutrons
options.B: Isotopes of chlorine have different atomic numbers but the same mass number
options.C: Chlorine has two stable isotopes, ^35Cl and ^37Cl, which differ in neutron number
options.D: Isotopes of chlorine differ in the number of electrons

mcqs.answer: Chlorine has two stable isotopes, ^35Cl and ^37Cl, which differ in neutron number
mcqs.explanation: Chlorine's stable isotopes ^35Cl (17 protons + 18 neutrons) and ^37Cl (17 protons + 20 neutrons) have the same atomic number but different neutron counts, giving different mass numbers. Options A and B are false, and D confuses isotopes with ions.

mcqs.question: Isobars are:

options.A: Atoms of the same element with different mass numbers
options.B: Atoms of different elements that have the same mass number
options.C: Atoms with the same number of protons but different neutrons
options.D: Atoms with the same number of neutrons but different protons

mcqs.answer: Atoms of different elements that have the same mass number
mcqs.explanation: Isobars are nuclides of different elements sharing the same mass number (total protons + neutrons). Option A describes isotopes, C also isotopes, and D is not a standard term.

mcqs.question: Which pair represents isotopes and which pair represents isobars?

options.A: Carbon-12 & Carbon-13 are isotopes; Carbon-12 & Nitrogen-12 are isobars
options.B: Carbon-12 & Nitrogen-12 are isotopes; Carbon-12 & Carbon-13 are isobars
options.C: Carbon-12 & Carbon-13 are isobars; Carbon-12 & Nitrogen-12 are isotopes

mcqs.answer: Carbon-12 & Carbon-13 are isotopes; Carbon-12 & Nitrogen-12 are isobars
mcqs.explanation: Isotopes are nuclides of the same element with different mass numbers (C‑12 and C‑13). Isobars are nuclides of different elements with the same mass number (C‑12 and N‑12 both have mass number 12). The other options mix up the definitions.
